lisbon.title: The 1980 Irpinia earthquake
lisbon.line: Rescuers took days to reach ruined villages in southern Italy, and President Pertini went on television to condemn the state’s failures.

lisbon.title: The 1988 Armenian earthquake
lisbon.line: At least 25,000 died in Soviet Armenia; shoddy Brezhnev-era buildings and slow rescues were blamed, deepening Armenians’ distrust of Moscow.

lisbon.title: The 1999 İzmit earthquake
lisbon.line: Over 17,000 died; anger at shoddy buildings and a disorganized state response helped sweep the ruling coalition from power in 2002.

luddites.title: Lancashire’s power-loom riots
luddites.line: Handloom weavers, impoverished by factory looms, smashed over 1,000 power looms across east Lancashire; troops shot six rioters dead.

luddites.title: US dockworkers strike over automation
luddites.line: About 45,000 dockworkers shut 36 East and Gulf Coast ports for three days, demanding higher pay and a full ban on automation.

cable.title: Roosevelt’s message circles the globe by cable
cable.line: A new Pacific cable via Hawaii reached Manila, and Roosevelt’s July 4 greeting became the first message sent around the world.

cable.title: The first transatlantic fiber-optic cable
cable.line: TAT-8 linked the US, Britain and France with glass fibers able to carry 40,000 calls, the first optical cable across an ocean.

cable.title: The Iridium satellite phone network
cable.line: Motorola-backed Iridium put 66 satellites in low orbit so phones could call from anywhere, but went bankrupt nine months after service began.

krakatoa.title: The volcanic winter of 536
krakatoa.line: A volcanic haze dimmed the sun for about 18 months; summers turned cold and harvests failed from Ireland to China.

krakatoa.title: Peru’s Huaynaputina erupts
krakatoa.line: South America’s largest recorded eruption chilled the Northern Hemisphere and is linked to the cold that brought Russia’s 1601–1603 famine.

krakatoa.title: Iceland’s ash cloud grounds Europe’s flights
krakatoa.line: Ash from Iceland’s Eyjafjallajökull closed much of Europe’s airspace for about a week, cancelling over 100,000 flights and stranding millions worldwide.

dreadnought.title: The Peloponnesian War begins
dreadnought.line: Thucydides wrote that the growth of Athens’ power, built on its navy, and the fear it caused in Sparta made war inevitable.

dreadnought.title: Japan abandons the naval treaty limits
dreadnought.line: Denied parity with Britain and the US, Japan gave notice it would leave the naval treaties, then secretly built giant battleships.

dreadnought.title: The Soviet Okean naval exercise
dreadnought.line: Admiral Gorshkov’s fast-growing Soviet fleet staged the largest peacetime naval exercise yet across several oceans, challenging US command of the seas.

somme.title: The Siege of Sevastopol
somme.line: Allied troops besieged Sevastopol for 11 months in trench lines fed by a new military railway, a foretaste of World War I.

somme.title: Korea’s trench stalemate
somme.line: From mid-1951 Korea’s front froze into trenches and hill battles like Pork Chop Hill, while jet fighters dueled overhead in “MiG Alley.”

somme.title: The Eritrea–Ethiopia border war
somme.line: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a trench war likened to World War I, with jet strikes and human-wave assaults; tens of thousands died.

crash.title: The Panic of 1857
crash.line: When a US railroad and land boom collapsed, panic spread to Britain and Europe in what is called the first worldwide crisis.

crash.title: Japan’s asset bubble bursts
crash.line: After a stock and property frenzy, Tokyo’s Nikkei peaked in December 1989 and lost about 60% by 1992, starting Japan’s “Lost Decade.”

crash.title: The Asian financial crisis
crash.line: Southeast Asia’s borrowing and property boom ended when Thailand’s baht collapsed, and panic spread to South Korea, Russia and Wall Street.

munich.title: Prussia and Austria seize Schleswig-Holstein
munich.line: Amid German nationalist calls to free German speakers from Danish rule, Prussia and Austria seized Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg from Denmark.

munich.title: Poland’s staged seizure of Vilnius
munich.line: Polish General Żeligowski staged a “mutiny” to take Lithuanian-claimed Vilnius, citing its Polish-speaking majority; Poland annexed the region in 1922.

munich.title: Serb rebels seize a third of Croatia
munich.line: As Croatia left Yugoslavia, Yugoslav army-backed Serb rebels took about a third of it, saying they were protecting Croatia’s Serbs.

mccarthy.title: The trial of Socrates
mccarthy.line: Athens sentenced Socrates to death for impiety and corrupting the young, charges colored by his questioning and his ties to oligarch Critias.

mccarthy.title: China’s Anti-Rightist Campaign
mccarthy.line: After Mao’s Hundred Flowers campaign invited criticism, over 550,000 people were branded “rightists” and many lost jobs or were sent to camps.

mccarthy.title: West Germany’s Radicals Decree
mccarthy.line: West Germany checked about 3.5 million people for public jobs; 1,250 were refused posts and 265 dismissed over alleged extremist ties.

protests.title: The anticolonial protests of 1919
protests.line: Hopes raised by Wilson’s talk of self-determination fed near-simultaneous protests in Korea, Egypt, India and China during the Paris peace talks.

protests.title: The Gen Z protest wave
protests.line: Youth-led protests spread from Indonesia and Nepal to Madagascar, Morocco and Peru, many under a One Piece anime flag, toppling two governments.

chernobyl.title: The Windscale reactor fire
chernobyl.line: Britain’s worst nuclear accident spread radioactive iodine; milk was dumped, and Macmillan censored the report to protect public confidence in nuclear power.

chernobyl.title: Japan’s Tokaimura nuclear accident
chernobyl.line: Workers mixing uranium in steel buckets set off a chain reaction that killed two, shaking Japanese trust in the nuclear industry.

deepblue.title: A program beats the backgammon world champion
deepblue.line: BKG 9.8 beat backgammon world champion Luigi Villa 7–1 in Monte Carlo, the first program to beat a reigning world champion.

deepblue.title: OpenAI Five beats Dota 2 world champions
deepblue.line: OpenAI’s bots beat OG, reigning world champions of the team video game Dota 2, two games to none in San Francisco.

deepblue.title: An AI drone outraces champion pilots
deepblue.line: The University of Zurich’s autonomous drone Swift beat three champion pilots in head-to-head races, a first for AI in a physical sport.
